cities.name: Lisbon
cities.local_food_tip: Try a fresh pastel de nata, caldo verde, grilled vegetables and baked breads with olive oil — Lisbon’s comfort classics.
cities.full_day: Morning: Explore Sé Cathedral’s exterior and wander Alfama’s narrow, colorful alleys. Enjoy a pastel de nata in a small local café. → Afternoon: Head to Belém for riverside views of Belém Tower and Jerónimos Monastery’s stunning façade. Have a Portuguese lunch with veggie-friendly options and take a relaxing walk along the Tagus promenade. → Sunset: Watch the city glow from Miradouro da Senhora do Monte. → Night: Stroll Praça do Comércio and the riverfront for soft lights, calm air and dessert shops.

ideas: Mild tram rides with scenic hill views.
Early mornings at the Belém waterfront.
Fresh juices in Alfama cool streets.
Warm colors in Graça and Alfama.
Pastel de nata with hot drinks by the river.

locations: Soft sunlight over Old Town rooftops.

public_transport_tips: Trams are perfect for hills but can be crowded — go earlier for easier rides.
Metro connects most neighborhoods quickly.
Walking in Alfama is best — streets are narrow and charming.
Use the Lisboa Viva or Viva Viagem card for cheaper rides.

cities.name: Porto
cities.local_food_tip: Taste veggie caldo verde, warm pastries and Mediterranean-style rice and veggie plates — Porto comfort food.
cities.full_day: Morning: Stroll Ribeira’s riverfront and walk up to the Sé Cathedral’s exterior for iconic views. Grab a pastry or juice by the Douro. → Afternoon: Cross the Dom Luís I Bridge (upper level) for huge panoramas, explore São Bento tiles, Livraria Lello’s exterior and Rua das Flores art street. Enjoy a veggie-friendly lunch. → Sunset: Relax at Jardim do Morro’s famous golden-hour viewpoint. → Night: Walk Gaia’s riverside promenade for dessert and calm reflections on the water.

ideas: Long sunsets from Jardim do Morro.
Craft shops in Rua das Flores.

public_transport_tips: The metro is great for long distances, especially across the river.
Ribeira is best explored on foot — narrow, scenic streets.
Trams along the river offer classic views.
Andante Card makes rides cheaper and simple.

city_events.name: São João Festival
city_events.description: Colorful decorations, music and fun coastal energy.

city_events.name: Porto Marathon
city_events.description: Scenic routes along the Douro with lots of cheer zones.

city_events.name: Christmas in Porto
city_events.description: Citywide lights, markets and cozy riverfront evenings.

cities.name: Braga
cities.local_food_tip: Try northern Portuguese veggie caldo verde, roasted vegetables, sweet pastries and salads — simple but comforting.
cities.full_day: Morning: Walk Braga Cathedral’s exterior and explore the old town’s tiled façades. Visit colorful gardens like Santa Barbara. → Afternoon: Head to Bom Jesus do Monte for its iconic staircase, lakes and viewpoints. Enjoy a light Minho-style lunch. → Sunset: Watch golden colors from Sameiro Sanctuary overlooking hills and forests. → Night: Stroll Avenida da Liberdade with fountains, dessert cafés and peaceful city lights.

ideas: Santa Barbara Garden in full flower.
Early hilltop visits to Bom Jesus.

locations: Holiday lights along Avenida da Liberdade.

public_transport_tips: Local buses connect Braga to Bom Jesus and Sameiro easily.
The old town is best explored on foot.
Taxis/ride apps are cheap for hilltop areas.
The train works great for regional connections.

city_events.name: Holy Week Celebrations
city_events.description: Braga’s most famous tradition with cultural performances.

city_events.name: Braga Summer Nights
city_events.description: Concerts, open-air shows and lively streets.

city_events.name: Christmas in Braga
city_events.description: Lights, markets and cozy decorated squares.

cities.name: Funchal (Madeira)
cities.local_food_tip: Taste sweet potatoes, veggie skewers, tropical fruits and soups — delicious island comfort food.
cities.full_day: Morning: Explore the Botanical Garden with tropical plants and bay views. Take the cable car for panoramic scenery, then stroll Monte’s peaceful upper town with a fresh hilltop café break. → Afternoon: Wander Funchal Old Town’s painted-door streets and browse fruit and flower stalls. Have a veggie-friendly island lunch and relax on the ocean promenade. → Sunset: Watch warm colors from Pico dos Barcelos viewpoint. → Night: Enjoy a calm marina walk with gelato, juices and ocean reflections.

ideas: Artisan craft corners with island charm.

public_transport_tips: Cable cars are perfect for reaching Monte.
Local buses cover most areas cheaply.
Walking in Old Town is ideal — small and scenic.
Promenade paths are wide and accessible.

city_events.name: Madeira Flower Festival
city_events.description: Massive floral displays and lively decorations.

city_events.name: Funchal Christmas Lights
city_events.description: Famous illuminated streets and festive markets.

cities.name: Ponta Delgada (Azores)
cities.local_food_tip: Try sweet potatoes, veggie stews, tropical fruits and plant-based island dishes — fresh and comforting.
cities.full_day: Morning: Explore Sete Cidades crater viewpoints and easy rim walks with fresh volcanic air. Enjoy a hilltop café stop. → Afternoon: Wander Ponta Delgada’s basalt old town, photograph Portas da Cidade and have a veggie-friendly Azorean lunch. Relax along the marina promenade. → Sunset: Head to Escalvado’s dramatic cliffside viewpoint. → Night: Enjoy a chill marina walk with waffles, fruit bowls and ocean reflections.

ideas: Fresh fruit stands in the city.
Quiet art streets in Old Town.

locations: Soft ocean air even in December.

public_transport_tips: Local buses connect major viewpoints and crater areas.
Old Town is walkable and compact.
Taxis help reach remote viewpoints more easily.
Marina area has wide accessible paths.

city_events.name: Azores Nature Festival
city_events.description: Outdoor activities celebrating the islands’ landscapes.

city_events.name: Summer by the Marina
city_events.description: Street arts, performers and seaside events.

city_events.name: Christmas in the Azores
city_events.description: Lights, decorations and cozy small-town charm.

cities.name: Angra do Heroísmo (Terceira)
cities.local_food_tip: Enjoy sweet potatoes, veggie soups, grilled vegetables and fresh island fruit — classic Terceira comfort food.
cities.full_day: Morning: Explore the UNESCO old town with pastel houses and basalt streets. Visit the Sé Cathedral exterior and relax in Duke of Terceira Garden. → Afternoon: Walk Monte Brasil’s forested volcanic trails and enjoy cliffside viewpoints like Miradouro da Quebrada with an island-style lunch nearby. → Sunset: Watch golden light spread across the bay from Miradouro do Facho. → Night: Take a peaceful Angra Bay walk with gelato, juices and gentle ocean breeze.

ideas: Fresh coastal trails in Monte Brasil.
Soft golden tones on hillside streets.

locations: Mild ocean breezes on promenade paths.
Holiday lights in Old Town squares.

public_transport_tips: Monte Brasil viewpoints are best reached by taxi or local buses.
Old Town is completely walkable.
Promenade paths are wide and accessible.
Rental e-bikes help with upper hills.

city_events.description: Island-wide celebrations with parades and performances.

city_events.description: Colorful dances and cultural events across the city.
